subject: iPhone: Keep favorite recaps and flyers
body: Pin favorite recaps and flyers to protect them from automatic cleanup. Each account keeps up to 100 recaps and 50 flyers, with pinned favorites and upcoming flyers protected; AI recap creation now offers text or a still illustration.

subject: iPhone: Game names ready when opening Other
body: Opening Other focuses Game name and shows saved game choices while the list refreshes. Game names load ahead of time, and the temporary Vollis-only choice no longer flashes while waiting.

subject: iPhone: Recent games first when adding an Other game
body: The Game name dropdown shows recent games first instead of sorting alphabetically. Saving a game moves its name to the top for the next entry.

subject: iPhone: Fewer interruptions when checking stats
body: Stats and game lists reuse recent results for five minutes, and adding, editing, or deleting a game prompts fresh results when you view them. Existing results stay visible while updates load, unrelated actions no longer restart stats loading, and you can still pull down to refresh anytime.

subject: iPhone: More room for stats while updating
body: Loading and updating messages now appear on one line in place of the Stats heading. The extra banner is gone, so refreshing stats leaves more room for results.

subject: iPhone: Matching dropdowns for game names and types
body: When adding an Other game, Game name and Game type show previous entries beneath the field, just like Winner 1. Type to narrow the choices, select an entry, or enter a new name or type.

subject: iPhone: Start the next doubles game at Winner 1
body: After saving a doubles game, the form clears and returns to Winner 1 with the keyboard and player choices ready for the next game.

subject: iPhone: Full names on games
body: Games show the person’s saved full name in the byline instead of a Google or Apple account ID.

subject: iPhone: Faster player choices when adding a game
body: Doubles player choices load ahead of time, and saved names appear immediately in Winner 1 and the other player fields while the list refreshes.

subject: iPhone: Share a recap from the top of the page
body: Tap Link at the top of an AI recap to copy its address and share it, including when signed in to a personal account. The link follows the recap you are currently viewing.

subject: iPhone: A cleaner way to browse and read AI recaps
body: Browse recaps in illustrated cards, whether signed in or signed out, and load older stories as you go. Recaps have larger reading text, more comfortable spacing, and colors that match your app appearance.

subject: iPhone: Flyers in Browse and Create
body: Signed-in personal accounts can now open Flyers under Browse and Flyer under Create in the More menu. Browse your saved flyers or start a new one from the same menu.

subject: iPhone: Choose previous games from the game name dropdown
body: In Add → Other, use the arrow beside Game name to see all previous game names. Vollis is included in the same list instead of appearing as a separate button, and you can still type a new game name.

subject: iPhone: Use your saved name after Apple sign-in
body: The app uses the name saved from Apple sign-in in the sign-in message and account menu, without asking you to enter a name. If no name is available, it simply shows Signed in.

subject: iPhone: Sign up again after an account is removed
body: Google and Apple sign-up can create a fresh account after the previous account was removed from the admin Users screen, instead of showing This account is inactive. The new account starts with its own empty game history.

subject: iPhone: Newest games first on player profiles
body: A player's doubles games appear from newest to oldest by when they were played, even when older games are entered later. Recent form and streaks also follow the game dates.

subject: iPhone: Faster return visits to stats and games
body: Previously viewed stats and game lists stay saved on your phone and appear while fresh results load. Recent results are reused to avoid repeated waits; pull down to refresh whenever you want the latest results.

subject: iPhone: More reliable Google sign-in
body: Google sign-in accepts small differences between Google’s clock and Stats, so a freshly completed sign-in is not rejected just because the clocks are a few seconds apart.

subject: iPhone: Clearer sign-in errors
body: If Google or Apple sign-in is rejected, the app shows the reason from Stats instead of only saying Please log in.

subject: iPhone: See when players are loading
body: The Players screen shows a spinner and Loading players message while it fetches the list, so you know players are on their way when you open it.

subject: iPhone: Your name instead of Apple account
body: If Apple did not share your name, use Add your name in the account menu to save it. Your name appears in the menu and stays saved for later sign-ins; use Edit name to change it.

subject: iPhone: KT Stats players when adding games
body: New accounts can choose KT Stats players when adding Doubles, Vollis, or Other games while KT Stats is enabled. Player suggestions follow your Stats to include choices, and games you add stay in your own account.

subject: iPhone: Names for Google and Apple accounts
body: Google and Apple sign-ins use your full name when it is provided, and keep it saved for later sign-ins. Stats to include also shows current users’ full names from their player profiles; KT Stats keeps its name.

subject: iPhone: Stats choices for existing and new accounts
body: Existing users start with all stats checked and can turn off sources or sharing whenever they want. New accounts, including Google and Apple sign-ins, can include KT Stats alongside their own games; other users’ stats stay out of their source list.

subject: iPhone: Your recaps and Kyle’s summaries
body: AI Recaps shows the recaps you created and includes Kyle’s summaries when KT Stats is enabled. Personal accounts can open recap links while signed in.

subject: iPhone: Your player name in the account menu
body: The account menu and sign-in greeting show your player name, such as Tyler Weston. Accounts without a matching player show a capitalized username.

subject: iPhone: The Oasis defaults for Tyler
body: When Tyler adds a game, the location starts as The Oasis. He can change it for games played elsewhere.

subject: iPhone: Choose whose stats to include
body: Your games stay in your own account. Use Stats to include to combine them with KT Stats or shared accounts, and choose whether other users can include yours. Kyle can include each user’s stats separately.

subject: iPhone: Clearer messages during an outage
body: When Stats is temporarily unavailable, the app shows a short message explaining when to try again instead of a page of server error text. If a game save is interrupted, the message reminds you to check your games before adding it again.

subject: iPhone: Voice game entry removed
body: The microphone shortcut and Doubles by voice menu option are gone. Add games using the player and score fields on the Add page.

subject: iPhone: Choose Vollis with your other games
body: In Add → Other, tap Game name to choose from all previous game names, including Vollis. The extra Other games/Vollis picker is gone; choosing Vollis sets up its players and scores and keeps games in your existing Vollis history.

subject: iPhone: Smoother stats loading and refresh
body: KT Stats load automatically after logging out, and recently viewed public stats appear immediately while fresh results load. A message at the top lets you keep browsing during loading; refresh stops with a retry message if the connection takes too long, keeping displayed stats available.

subject: iPhone: Clear feedback when deleting games
body: Deleting a game immediately shows a spinner and a Deleting game message. When deletion succeeds, the game disappears and Game deleted confirms it; if it fails, an error explains what happened.

subject: iPhone: Consistent background updates while you browse
body: Game saves, AI recaps, flyers, AI characters, and changes waiting to sync use matching green status messages at the top. Saving shows your game immediately and lets you browse other pages while it finishes; errors appear in red and failed saves keep your entries.

subject: iPhone: Simpler Add page and Menu
body: Add now shows Doubles and Other, with Vollis inside Other. In More, browse players, AI recaps, and flyers, create an AI recap or flyer, or add a doubles game by voice.

subject: iPhone: Sign up again after deleting your account
body: After deleting your account, you can use the same Apple or Google sign-in to create a fresh account. Your deleted games stay deleted, and your old account stays closed.

subject: iPhone: A single Menu heading
body: Opening More shows Menu at the top, with the duplicate heading removed.

subject: iPhone: Browse AI recaps without logging in
body: When signed out, open More → AI Recaps to browse published recaps and subscribe by email on the same page. No account is needed.

subject: iPhone: Game times and cleaner game cards
body: Game lists show the saved time beside each game's date when available. The faint lines through and between game cards are gone.

subject: iPhone: Return to Stats while your AI summary generates
body: Submitting an AI summary takes you back to Stats with a generating message. Keep browsing while it works, then tap Open recap when it is ready.

subject: iPhone: See the game you just added
body: After adding a game, a popup shows the players, scores, and any location or comments. Tap outside or Done to close it, or choose Add another game to start the next entry.

subject: iPhone: Large win and loss totals stay readable
body: Standings give wins and losses enough room for larger totals, including counts over 1,000. Numbers stay on one line and lined up beneath their headings.

subject: iPhone: Cleaner login and personal AI tools
body: Google sign-in has a full-width button, and the choice between your stats and KT Stats lives in More. Personal accounts can edit their players’ photos, signature looks, and AI characters and create AI summaries of their games.

subject: iPhone: Today’s differential stays visible
body: Today’s standings keep names and numbers on the same line, with wins and losses closer together so the +/− differential stays visible without swiping sideways. Names that do not fit end with an ellipsis.

subject: iPhone: Player names stay on one line
body: Today’s and yearly standings have smaller side margins and keep player names on one line. Names that do not fit end with an ellipsis; tap a player to open their full details.

subject: iPhone: A simpler More menu
body: When signed out, More shows Home, Appearance, AI Recaps, and Login. Tournaments and Player Network have been removed from More, personal accounts no longer show Volleyball there, and AI Summary is available from Add.

subject: iPhone: Personal accounts and private stats
body: Create a personal account with a password, Apple, or Google to keep your own games, players, and stats separate from everyone else's.

subject: iPhone: Explore KT Stats before getting started
body: Browse KT Stats without changing its games or players, then create an account for your own games. Hide or show KT Stats whenever you like; nothing is deleted.

subject: iPhone: More room for stats and games
body: The year menu now sits at the top left of Stats and Games, leaving more room for search and results.

subject: iPhone: Browse AI recaps without logging in
body: Open More, then AI Recaps to read published recaps without an account. Choose Subscribe by email to sign up for future recap emails.

subject: iPhone: Choose your colors and style
body: Open More, then Appearance to choose Ocean, Forest, Sunset, or Violet colors and Classic, Soft, or Sharp styling. Light and dark modes and your appearance choices apply immediately and stay saved on your iPhone.

subject: iPhone: Simpler Games navigation
body: Removed the duplicate Games button at the top left of Stats. Open Games from the tab at the bottom of the screen.

subject: iPhone: Open players from Sequence standings
body: Tapping a player in Sequence or other game standings opens their stats without a Server Double-Fault error. Player totals and opponent records include team games and games with multiple opponents.

subject: iPhone: Remember the latest game's player count
body: After saving an Other game such as Sequence, the next entry for that game uses the number of winners and losers you just entered. Saving a two-player game now replaces the extra player fields from an earlier three- or four-player game.

subject: iPhone: Faster setup for Other games
body: Choosing a known game such as No jump fills in its game type, scoring, and player slots immediately. You can start entering players while suggestions load.

subject: iPhone: Select your recent games for AI summaries
body: Select all chooses every game you added on your latest game day, even when other people have added newer games. The selection includes the whole day without cutting off longer sessions.

subject: iPhone: Choose one player to animate
body: Choose the one player who moves in an animated recap and describe a simple action just for them. The animation keeps everyone else in the starting picture still.

subject: iPhone: Animated AI recaps
body: Choose With animation when creating an AI recap and describe what the players should do. A short, silent animation uses the same player references and appears in place of the recap picture.

subject: iPhone: Edited games keep their original time
body: Editing a doubles or Vollis game keeps its original date and time, so it stays in the same place in game history. This also applies to doubles edits saved offline and synced later.

subject: iPhone: Cleaner stats and game browsing
body: Browse games sits beside Men’s and Women’s, with Doubles, Vollis, and No jump grouped under Volleyball. Doubles opens the current year, other games choose their only recorded year or All years, and Games opens the current game’s list; ratings show numbers without P markers and include supported multiplayer results.

subject: iPhone: Ratings for today’s doubles
body: Today’s doubles standings show ratings based only on that day’s games, with less weight given to a one-game result. Group AI pictures request a king or queen based on the highest rating in the selected session.

subject: iPhone: Tuck away game choices
body: In Other stats and games, selecting a game tucks away the game buttons so results are easier to see. Tap Change game to reopen the choices, just like on the website.

subject: iPhone: Other games show all years
body: Other games, including No Jump and Vollis, start with all years of results. You can still choose a year, and Doubles keeps its own year selection.

subject: iPhone: Ratings for more games
body: No Jump, Vollis, and other supported games have separate skill ratings alongside wins and losses. Early ratings are marked provisional, and results without clear teams stay in your stats without affecting ratings.

subject: iPhone: Find No Jump and other games faster
body: Choose a game directly in Other stats and games. No Jump and Vollis are grouped under Volleyball, with game choices visible above the results.

subject: iPhone: Roomier AI prompts and remembered game locations
body: AI summary and image prompts have room for paragraphs, sentence capitalization, and autocorrect and predictive suggestions when enabled in your keyboard settings. New games keep the location from your last saved game on this device, separately for each user.

subject: iPhone: More room for game comments
body: Game comments have a larger text box that grows as you write, with room for paragraphs and line breaks. Comments use sentence capitalization and allow autocorrect and predictive suggestions when enabled in your iPhone keyboard settings.

subject: iPhone: More rows and roomier player names
body: Lists show 25 items before Extend appears. Game cards take up less space, and tighter stats columns give player names more room before wrapping.

subject: iPhone: Shorter lists and tighter page spacing
body: Long lists show the first five items, with Extend to reveal the rest and Show less to shorten them again. Search sits closer to Stats and Games, keeping more useful content on screen.

subject: iPhone: Connected headers and a consistent look
body: Stats headers and their rows now share one rounded card. Games, player details, game entry, More, and admin sections use the same connected layout, and ratings show two decimal places.

subject: iPhone: A refreshed look for standings and games
body: Standings and games have rounded cards, clearer scores, and collapsible headers with player and game counts. Tap a header for a springy open-and-close effect, with gentler transitions when Reduce Motion is enabled.

subject: iPhone: A fresh form after saving a game
body: Saving a game clears the entry fields, including location, and returns you to the first field for the next game. This also works after updating a game; unsuccessful saves keep your entries.

subject: iPhone: Finished AI summaries open automatically
body: When your AI summary finishes while you are on the creation screen, the recap opens automatically in the app. This works for both text-only summaries and summaries with illustrations.

subject: iPhone: Back from a player returns to Games
body: On Games, after you open a player, Back takes you to the games you were looking at instead of another player.

subject: iPhone: move on to the next game after saving
body: Confirmed saves clear the player and score fields for the next game. If confirmation is lost, Doubles and Vollis check whether the game was saved without submitting it again. If the result is still uncertain, your entries stay in place with a clearer message.

subject: iPhone: hide the keyboard more easily
body: Tap Done at the bottom right of the text keyboard to hide it. When entering scores, use the hide-keyboard button on the right above the number keys.

subject: iPhone: more room to choose players
body: The field you are filling in moves toward the top, scrolling the Add heading and shortcut buttons out of the way. This leaves more room for player suggestions in Doubles, Vollis, and Other games.
